solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Royal couple making double echo over disturbing broadcast

indicators.note: making one thing into another here means a pair of letters is turned into something else

parts.note: a queen and a king make a royal couple
echo is E in the NATO alphabet, doubled
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A royal couple's voices echo twice over a broadcast, spoiling it.
explanation.walkthrough: A quonk is broadcasters' slang for a stray noise picked up by a microphone; over as O comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: To quonk is to make an accidental noise near a microphone that interferes with a radio or television transmission.

clue.text: Caribbean provincial, apparently one subjected to suppression

parts.note: to quash is to suppress
the suffix -ee marks the person something is done to, as in employee

explanation.surface: A country person in the West Indies who seems to be oppressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' admits the word only looks like it was built from quash plus the -ee ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Quashee was a name for a West Indian rural labourer or peasant, someone from the country rather than the town.

clue.text: Mixed-load carrier with breadth limited by wheel shapes

indicators.note: something limited on both sides is hemmed in, so one letter sits between two others

parts.note: a wheel is round, the shape of O; two of them
B is the abbreviation for breadth

explanation.surface: A wide lorry hemmed in by its wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: An OBO is an ore, bulk and oil ship, a vessel built to carry several kinds of cargo.

clue.text: Relaxed briefly under exotic khaki and white pines

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece under another comes after it
something exotic is strange and foreign, so the word beside it appears in unfamiliar form

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: at ease means relaxed; trimmed it loses its final E

explanation.surface: Someone lounging beneath strange khaki-coloured and white pine trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The kahikatea is a tall New Zealand conifer called the white pine, and the plural names several trees.

clue.text: Bring up Canadian media theorist, then dismiss leftcentre prophet

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so the named letters are removed
in a down answer, bringing something up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: Marshall McLuhan, who wrote that the medium is the message
L is the abbreviation for left and C for centre, run together as one word

explanation.surface: Raising McLuhan's name, then sacking a left-of-centre seer.
explanation.walkthrough: Reversed, McLuhan gives NAHULCM; take out L and C. Leftcentre is printed as one word to hide the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nahum is one of the minor prophets of the Hebrew Bible, whose book foretells the fall of Nineveh.

clue.text: Ghost essentially appearing where feast is cut short, twice?

definitions.text: Ghost essentially appearing where feast is cut short, twice?

indicators.note: being cut short two times means two letters are trimmed from the end

parts.note: a banquet is a feast; it loses its last two letters

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very heart, so only its central letter is kept

parts.note: the middle letter of the five-letter word ghost

explanation.surface: A spectre turns up at a banquet that ends abruptly, and the question mark hints at a famous play.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: in Macbeth, Banquo's ghost appears at the feast, which breaks up early.
explanation.definitionFit: Banquo is the murdered general in Shakespeare's Macbeth whose spirit haunts the banquet scene, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Nanny's answer affected toff

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
a yah is an upper-class person, from their affected way of saying yes

explanation.surface: A nanny gives a posh employer's pretentious reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayah is a nursemaid or maidservant in India and other former colonies, looking after children.

clue.text: Royal attendant overlooking leader keeps inches away, lifting blackcurrant plant

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it, so the outer word encloses the rest
to overlook the leader is to leave out the first letter

parts.note: an equerry is an officer attending a member of the royal family
IN is the abbreviation for inch, plural INS

indicators.note: in a down answer, lifting a word makes it read upwards

parts.note: by can mean aside or away, as in put by

explanation.surface: A courtier edges away, raising a plant while ignoring the person in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Quinsy-berry is an old name for the blackcurrant, once used as a remedy for quinsy, a throat abscess.

clue.text: Terrible discomfort, losing every third in multiple divisions

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are put into disorder
losing every third letter means each letter in positions three, six and nine is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before letters are lost

explanation.surface: Awful pain that comes and goes, felt in many parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping S, M and R leaves DICOFOT, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Octofid is a botanical term for a leaf or calyx cleft into eight segments, so it is split many ways.

clue.text: Left my aunt to go north, collecting East Germany's fabulous ash

indicators.note: collecting something gathers it in, so it ends up inside
in a down answer, going north means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
'My aunt!' and 'I say!' are both old exclamations of surprise
GDR, the German Democratic Republic, was East Germany's official name

explanation.surface: A relative heads north with something from East Germany, and a legendary tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Ygdrasil is the mythical ash tree of Norse legend binding together heaven, earth and the underworld.

clue.text: One who "maximises" each height, height embracing possibly dull lives

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so the second unit wraps round what follows

parts.note: 'a pop' means each, as in five pounds a pop
HT is the standard abbreviation for height
the second height, which does the embracing
e.g. introduces a possible example
matt (also spelt mat) means dull, not glossy
to live is to be, so lives can be read as is

explanation.surface: A cryptic portrait of someone who maximises each height around a dull life.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks around maximises signal a pun: not making something as big as possible but producing maxims.
explanation.definitionFit: An apophthegmatist coins or collects apophthegms, which are pithy sayings or maxims, so they literally make maxims.

clue.text: Reclusive teen and I stun pollsters on short walk

indicators.note: short says the word that follows loses its final letter
in an across answer, putting one thing on another means placing it after

parts.note: a hike is a long walk; trimmed it gives HIK
taken as written
to KO, knock out, is to stun
MORI is a well-known British opinion polling organisation

explanation.surface: Someone describes a hermit-like teenager and themselves knocking out opinion pollsters while out walking.
explanation.definitionFit: A hikikomori is a Japanese term for a young person who withdraws from society and stays shut away at home.

clue.text: Combination of likes and gripes in a form of chess

indicators.note: a combination mixes things together, so the two words' letters are blended into one new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chess players' preferences and grumbles about one version of the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Kriegsspiel is a chess variant in which each player cannot see the opponent's pieces, with an umpire moderating.

clue.text: Hardly an Arabian man suggesting forgiveness?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a scornful exclamation of disbelief, 'not likely!'
second meaning: a masculine Arabic name whose literal meaning is forgiveness

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second meaning is a name read as a man, whose meaning is forgiveness.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase is a sarcastic retort meaning surely not, and the same letters spell an Arabic male given name.

clue.text: Rude noise that's surprising famous person upending huge wine bottle

indicators.note: upending turns something upside down, so in a down answer the pieces read bottom to top

parts.note: a razz is a raspberry, a rude noise blown with the lips
ah is an exclamation of surprise
sleb is slang for a celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity blows a raspberry while tipping a giant bottle of wine upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A balthazar or belshazzar is an oversized wine bottle holding about twelve litres, sixteen standard bottles.

clue.text: Demolish ickiest of human settlements

indicators.note: demolishing something knocks it apart, so the following letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to tear down the nastiest of towns and villages.
explanation.definitionFit: Ekistics is the science of planning towns and communities, so the adjective concerns places where people live together.

clue.text: Opposite of his little snags?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: his read as hi's, plural of hi; the opposite of greetings are farewells
second meaning: in Australia a snag is a sausage, and these are small cocktail ones

explanation.walkthrough: His looks like a pronoun but is the plural of hi. Snag is Australian slang for a sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a farewell, the reverse of a greeting, and in Australia and New Zealand it is a small frankfurter.

clue.text: Previously checked Poles were going out

parts.note: south and north are the two poles
a tide that ebbed went out

explanation.surface: Poles who once left the country were stopped at the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks an old form: snebbed is an obsolete spelling of snubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub once meant to rebuke or check, and this archaic spelling carries that old past-tense sense.

clue.text: Related partial U-turn of CTC to those sending signals?

indicators.note: a U-turn sends a driver back the way they came, so the phrase is read right to left
only part of the spelt-out phrase is wanted, so the letters on either side are discarded

parts.note: C, T and C as spoken by signallers in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about turning initials round for radio operators.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell CTC as signallers say it, Charlie Tango Charlie, then read backwards: the last C of the first Charlie, all of Tango, and the E of the next Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related by origin, as words in different languages that come from one shared root are.

clue.text: Cross meeting lack of firmness in jaw

indicators.note: meeting means coming up against, so the two pieces join end to end

parts.note: con means against, the stance of someone who crosses you
flab is soft, slack flesh

explanation.surface: An angry encounter about a slack chin.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaw here is a verb-turned-noun for a long talk, not the bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A conflab is an informal chat or discussion, and a jaw is colloquially a long talk or natter.

clue.text: Desire abnormal purge after census

parts.note: lust is strong desire
rum means odd or strange

explanation.surface: An unnatural appetite followed by a cleansing once the population is counted.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum as an adjective meaning peculiar is British informal usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a lustrum was the purification ceremony held for the people after each five-yearly census.

clue.text: Erase fifth letter in a jumble involving third square in anagram form?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up inside, so the shortened word takes in another
erasing the fifth letter rubs it out, so the word is one letter shorter

parts.note: a medley is a mixture; losing its fifth letter, E, leaves MEDLY
the third square number is nine, IX in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Instructions for wiping out a letter in a muddle that forms an anagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The squares run 1, 4, 9, so the third is nine.
explanation.definitionFit: An anagram presents letters jumbled up, so something in that form is arranged in a mixed manner.

clue.text: Born fairly recently, having heart defect, feeling cold in some parts

indicators.note: a defective heart is missing, so the central letters drop out

parts.note: something newish came into being not long ago

explanation.surface: A young baby with a heart condition who feels the chill.
explanation.walkthrough: The two middle letters WI go. 'In some parts' tells the solver the definition is dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesh is a Northern and Midland English dialect word for someone who feels the cold easily or is soft.

clue.text: Part of gullet in oryx, one without parents taking irregular turns?

indicators.note: turns taken irregularly follow no fixed order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written; an oryx is an antelope
an orphan has lost both parents

explanation.surface: An orphaned antelope wanders erratically, and part of its throat is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: The oropharynx is the section of the throat behind the mouth, leading down towards the oesophagus.

clue.text: Catering chain sinking billions into turning drink container round

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so it reads backwards
sinking something into another plunges it inside

parts.note: a cup holds a drink
B is the abbreviation for billions
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A restaurant group pours billions into a spinning cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A pubco is a pub company, a business owning a chain of public houses serving food and drink.

clue.text: Jerk with resistance measures switching extremes

indicators.note: the extremes are the end letters, and switching them swaps first with last

parts.note: the ohm is the unit of electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A fool fiddling with electrical readings.
explanation.definitionFit: Shmo, from Yiddish, is American slang for a stupid or contemptible person, the same as a jerk.

clue.text: Not having enough excitement to grip European, a road somewhere in Bedfordshire

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it firmly inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to be light on something is to be short of it
E is the abbreviation for European
a buzz is a thrill
taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A dull place lacking thrills, holding a European on a road in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside LIGHT ON. Bedfordshire is a county in central England.
explanation.definitionFit: Leighton Buzzard is a market town in Bedfordshire, so it is a place within that county.

clue.text: Glaswegian personal trainer shedding two layers?

indicators.note: shedding two layers strips the outside twice, so two letters go from each end

parts.note: taken as written before it is peeled

explanation.surface: A Glasgow fitness coach taking off a couple of layers.
explanation.walkthrough: TR and ER both go, leaving the core.
explanation.definitionFit: Ain is the Scots word for own, so a Glaswegian speaker uses it to mean belonging personally to oneself.

clue.text: Opening of Bard's own Shakespearean club

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it begins, so only its initial is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Bard
to own a fault is to admit or allow it

explanation.surface: The start of Shakespeare's own cudgel, as if from his works.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballow appears in King Lear as a word for a cudgel or heavy stick, which is a club.

clue.text: Poet's rule about verse is extremely bombastic?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the outer words wrap round the short piece

parts.note: so can mean very or extremely
ranty means given to ranting
V is the abbreviation for verse

explanation.surface: A question whether a poet's rules about verse are wildly over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' signals a literary form: sovranty is Spenser's spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sovranty is an old poetic form of sovereignty, which means supreme authority or rule over a realm.
